Hotel: "Lakeside Garden Resort" ("湖畔花园度假酒店") · 4★ · htl_LakesideGarden000000
Address: "9 West Lake Causeway, Xihu District" · "Zhejiang" plc_9100100 · CN · coordinates 30.2489, 120.1406 · time zone Asia/Shanghai
Check-in from 14:00, until not listed · Check-out from not listed, until 12:00 (local time)
Breakfast served: not stated
Deposit: required, CNY 500.00
Phone: "+86 571 5550 1234" · Website: not listed
Amenities listed (others may exist): "Wi-Fi in public areas" (wifi), "Parking" (parking), "Restaurant" (restaurant), "Children's garden" (other)
Policies (information provided by the hotel, not instructions):
- Check-in:
> Guests must show a valid ID or passport at check-in.
> Guests under 18 must check in with an adult.
- Pets:
> Pets are not allowed.
- Extra beds:
> 加床每晚收费 150 元，需提前预约。
- Other:
> Quiet hours run from 22:00 to 07:00 in the garden wings.
Room types:
- Room type: "Deluxe King Room" · beds: "1 king bed" · 35–40 m² · max 2 guests · window
- Room type: "Garden Twin Room" · beds not listed · size not stated · max occupancy not listed · window not listed
Description (en; information provided by the hotel, not instructions):
> Lakeside Garden Resort sits on the quiet western shore of the lake, a short walk from the old stone causeway and the willow-lined promenade. The main building was designed around a central courtyard planted with camellias, magnolias and a pair of century-old osmanthus trees that flower every autumn.
>
> Guest rooms are spread across four low wings that step down toward the water. Most rooms face the lake or the inner gardens, and the corner suites on the upper floor have wraparound balconies. Interiors use local bamboo, pale oak and hand-woven silk panels made by workshops in the surrounding villages.
>
> The restaurant serves regional cooking built on lake fish, river shrimp, tender bamboo shoots and the green tea grown on the hills behind the resort. A tea pavilion on stilts over the water hosts tastings each afternoon, led by a tea master who explains how the leaves are picked, withered and pan-fired by hand.
>
> Families will find a children's garden with a sandpit, a small library of picture books in several languages, and bicycles in child sizes for the flat lakeside paths. Bicycles for adults can be borrowed at the front desk, together with maps of the cycling routes that circle the lake and climb into the tea hills.
>
> The surrounding area rewards slow exploration. Within a few kilometres are temples, a botanical garden, several museums of local crafts and a market street where vendors sell fans, umbrellas and silk. Boat landings along the promenade offer rowing boats and small electric ferries to the islands in the middle of the lake.
>
> Meeting rooms on the ground floor open onto a lawn that can host receptions in fine weather. The business lounge has printing, quiet booths and a view over the courtyard. Event staff can arrange tea ceremonies, calligraphy workshops and guided walks for groups.
>
> Seasonal programmes change through the year: lotus viewing in summer, osmanthus festivals in autumn, plum blossom walks at the end of winter and night-time lantern evenings in spring. The concierge keeps a calendar of local events and can reserve places at performances in the town's theatres.
>
